summary.value: Dialog component, used to display a dialog dialog.

example.value:
<Dialog.TriggerContext>
  <Dialog.Trigger>Open Dialog</Dialog.Trigger>
  <Dialog>
    <Dialog.Block>
      Content
    </Dialog.Block>
  </Dialog>
</Dialog.TriggerContext>

@example without TriggerContext
const dialogRef = useRef<HTMLDialogElement>(null);

...

<Button command="show-modal" commandfor="my-dialog">Open Dialog</Button>
<Dialog id="my-dialog">
  Content
</Dialog>

a11y.method: drafted from the docs page, quote-verified, human-reviewed 2026-08-11 (batch 2: agent first-pass, ratified)

value.rule: Make sure elements receiving focus are not hidden behind the dialog
value.quote: Note: Make sure that elements receiving focus are not hidden behind the dialog .

value.rule: Add aria-haspopup="dialog" to the element that opens the dialog so screen reader users know it will open a dialog
value.quote: The attribute aria-haspopup="dialog" should be added to the element that opens the dialog to make it clear to screen reader users that it will open a dialog.

value.rule: Always provide a visible and simple way to close a dialog
value.quote: Always ensure that users have a visible and simple way to close a dialog.

value.rule: The close button (X) should stay visible even when the dialog's content requires scrolling
value.quote: The most common approach is a close button (X) in the top right corner. It should remain visible even when the dialog contains a lot of content and the user needs to scroll.

value.rule: In non-modal dialogs, elements receiving keyboard focus must not end up hidden behind the dialog
value.quote: When using non-modal dialogs, you must ensure that elements receiving focus through keyboard navigation do not end up behind the dialog and become hidden. See criteria 2.4.11 (w3.org) (AA) and 2.4.12 (w3.org) (AAA).

value.rule: Focusable elements must never be completely covered by the dialog during Tab navigation
value.quote: Ensure that focusable elements are never completely covered by the dialog when users navigate the page using the Tab key.

value.rule: Focus order must be logical and focus must always be visible
value.quote: Ensure that the focus order is logical and that focus is always visible, so users navigating with a keyboard or screen reader can understand where focus is located.

value.rule: Esc closes the dialog and returns focus to the trigger
value.quote: Esc closes the dialog (focus returns to the trigger)

relations.method: drafted from the docs page, quote-verified, human-reviewed 2026-08-11 (batch 2: agent first-pass, ratified)

value.note: Use alert instead of a modal dialog when notifying users of something that does not require action
value.quote: you need to notify users about something that does not require action. Use alert or a non-modal dialog instead

value.note: Use popover instead of a modal dialog for short, optional information
value.quote: you want to provide short, optional information, use popover

value.note: Consult the system notifications pattern for guidance on when a modal dialog should be used
value.quote: See also the system notifications pattern for more guidance on when a modal dialog should be used.

composition.method: drafted from the docs page, quote-verified, human-reviewed 2026-08-11 (batch 2: agent first-pass, ratified)

value.rule: Using the placement prop, a dialog can behave like a drawer positioned from a given side
value.quote: Using placement , dialog can behave like a so-called “drawer” from the position you specify.

value.rule: Use multiple ds-dialog__block elements to divide the dialog with dividers into separate areas
value.quote: Use multiple ds-dialog__block if you want to divide the dialog with dividers into, for example, a top and bottom area.

value.rule: Content cannot be placed directly in the dialog if ds-dialog__block is used; all content must then be inside a block
value.quote: Note that content cannot be placed directly in dialog if you use ds-dialog__block ; then all content should be inside one of the dialog's ds-dialog__block sections.

value.rule: A close button that is the dialog's first direct child floats to the top right
value.quote: If the button is a direct child of the dialog and the first element, it will float to the top right.

value.rule: Use Dialog.TriggerContext together with Dialog.Trigger so the dialog and trigger can communicate without id/commandfor
value.quote: Use Dialog.TriggerContext and Dialog.Trigger together, so Dialog can communicate without having to use id and commandfor .

value.rule: Use buttons in the dialog to give users a clear path forward
value.quote: Use buttons to give users a clear path forward.
